title: When, My Saviour, Shall I Be
description: When, My Saviour, Shall I Be in Tonic Solfa to PLEYEL'S HYMN, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 381.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Sevens (7.7.7.7), and this page sets them to PLEYEL'S HYMN; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: When, my Sa-viour, shall I be Per-fect-ly re-signed to thee Poor and vile in my own eyes, On-ly in thy wis-dom wise!

lines: When, my Saviour, shall I be
Poor and vile in my own eyes,
So I may thy Spirit know,
Let him as he listeth blow;
So I may with thee be one.
All the depths of humble love!

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to PLEYEL'S HYMN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
